- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) and forecast spikes upward, cap the forecast at 1.5x the recent 7-day average to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and forecast is low, add 0.2–0.5 to the forecast to counteract underestimation.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price declining steadily), reduce forecast by 10–20% to avoid overreacting to recent lows.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is erratic, use the 14-day moving average as a smoothing anchor instead of the 30-day trend.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >20% and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, assume market is “overcorrecting” — reduce next forecast by 15–30% to avoid future overestimation.
- For forecasts with high volatility (e.g., >30% deviation from true outcome), apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment is positive, use 70% of forecast + 30% of true; if negative, use 30% of forecast + 70% of true.
